BEFORE PROPOSING, AUDIT: which other Pydantic request models in hub/hub/schemas/ and hub/hub/api/v1/ allow extras, and is the lax setting a default or a choice? The route is not publicly documented as tolerant, the only known clients are the Hub's own UI and this repo's harnesses, and the failure it prevents is an unsupervised run the operator believes is supervised. carried_open_questions: F131 (new, iteration 11): POST /conversations/{id}/continue resolves the conversation ONLY to 404 on it, then calls schedule_agent(project_id, conversation.agent) (hub/hub/api/v1/checkpoints.py:271), which starts the AGENT's next queued entry whatever conversation it belongs to -- and returns {'conversation_id': <the one you pressed>, 'started': true}. Measured twice with different ids: a cutover left one entry queued for a successor, Continue was pressed on a DIFFERENT open conversation of the same agent with nothing queued for it, and the answer was started:true against the pressed conversation while the successor's entry was consumed and the run landed on the successor (confirmed against the runs table). The scheduling is right; the ANSWER is false, and an operator watching the conversation they pressed sees success then nothing. Same family as F116 and F128. Smallest fix: return the conversation id of the entry actually picked. Driven by scripts/drive/t_continue_branches.py, 16/16.

F130 (new, iteration 11): pressing Checkpoint twice with no turn in between makes EVERY later checkpoint in that conversation re-summarise it from turn one. The empty-span checkpoint answers 201/ready/probe passed and stores covers_through_run_id = NULL (checkpoints.py:367, `runs[-1].id if runs else None`); runs_to_cover reads NULL as 'unknown, cover everything' (checkpoints.py:179). Measured on two independent chains: checkpoint #3's files_changed names CHAIN_ONE.txt, which #1 already covered, alongside the new CHAIN_TWO.txt. In the first run the re-covered body opened 'No progress... the file has not been created' while its own computed half listed that file -- so the cost is not only worker price on a long conversation but a checkpoint that contradicts itself. The probe passes correctly; it grades a blind reader's recovery, not truth. One NULL is carrying two meanings ('I do not know where you got to' and 'exactly where the last one did') and only the first is handled. Three fix shapes costed in FINDINGS.md F130; the cheapest is one line. Wants a spec loop. Driven by scripts/drive/t_row15_chain.py, 25/25.

F129 (new, iteration 10): requirement drift is correct and the app cannot reach any of it. Driven end to end for the first time (row 10, scripts/drive/t_row10_drift.py, 31/31): evidence footprints on the right branch and commit, a change to a footprinted file raises exactly one candidate naming that file, coverage moves to `drifting` and back to `verified`, the resolution holds against a re-scan, a further change raises a fresh row, and putting the file back to its footprinted blob raises nothing. But POST /spec/drift/detect is the ONLY writer of a RequirementDrift row -- no scheduler sweep, no MCP tool, no second route -- and hub/ui/src never calls it: `drift` survives in the UI only as the WORD `drifting` in api/spec.ts:98 and SpecCoverageBar.tsx:10. So the coverage bar has a bucket that cannot light up through the app, and if anything outside the app lights it up, `drifting` sits at the TOP of the coverage precedence and that requirement reads drifting on every screen permanently, with no way to see what moved and no way to answer. It is a UI gap, not a backend one. The one judgement worth the operator's time: whether the scan stays a manual button (it runs git ls-tree per branch plus a reachability refresh, and the route's own comment says the explicit scan is also when reachability is re-answered) or acquires a cadence -- recommendation is the button first.

F127 (new, iteration 9): pressing Run on a healthy loop whose agent is mid-turn answers 500 "Failed to fire job" with no reason and no JobRun row. The busy guard (_loop_flow_busy_reason) records nothing by design, and F48 re-derivation in run_job cannot see it because _loop_work_is_all_in_flight asks decide_firing, which never reaches the guard. Reproduced deterministically, 7/7, in scripts/drive/t_run_while_busy2.py. The honest fix is to make the re-derivation consult the busy guard too and answer 409 naming the busy agent; the tempting narrow fix (treat "no row written" as "nothing is wrong") is the exact inference F48 argues against. Wants a spec loop; cron firings are unaffected, this is only the manual Run button.

F128 (new, iteration 9): a loop runs on an agent its job does not name. _agents_that_are_free is PROJECT-scoped, so the busy guard refuses only when every sibling is also occupied; otherwise the firing proceeds and staffs whoever is free. Measured: job configured agent gamma, gamma mid-turn, Run pressed -> 200 and alpha did the work, with alpha as the task assignee. The docstring invariant ("its one agent is the busy one and the free list is empty") only holds in a one-agent project. NOT filed as a defect: design D12 chose width for flows and job.agent is D2 default. It is one operator decision with two shapes -- make the free list loop-scoped, or stop presenting job.agent as who runs this loop.

F126 (new, iteration 8): a spent checkpoint can be cut over again. POST /checkpoints/{id}/cutover guards only on checkpoint.status != 'ready' and on archivable(predecessor), whose first line returns None for an already-archived conversation -- so a second press returns 200 and mints a second successor. Driven live: two open 'handoff' conversations with the IDENTICAL derived title, and the duplicate entry was DELIVERED in its own run, so a whole billed Haiku turn was spent rediscovering that the work was done. The only thing stopping this today is client-side and per-tab (checkpointOperationStore's inFlight map); the Hub's own standard is a server-side claim, which take_checkpoint has and cutover does not. Three shapes costed in FINDINGS.md; recommendation is a Checkpoint.cut_over_to_conversation_id column (one migration) because it also answers 'where did this checkpoint go', which nothing can answer today. Decide alongside the second half of the finding: the UI's cutover banner filters on trigger === 'context_pressure', so a checkpoint the operator generated on purpose is never offered a cutover anywhere in the UI.

F124 (new, iteration 7): a loop's work can never reach the main branch. Integration resolves its commit through TaskRequirementLink -> RequirementEvidence (accepted) -> EvidenceFootprint, and a loop's initial_tasks carry no requirement links, so record_evidence has nothing to name and NOTHING_TO_MERGE is permanent rather than 'a state of the world'. The card offers 'Try again' anyway and appends an identical skipped row, while integration-preview already knows will_merge is false. Three shapes costed in FINDINGS.md; recommendation is the smallest one (stop offering the retry) now and the honest one (let a loop produce evidence) as its own change. NOT F122 -- that task had evidence awaiting acceptance.

F125 (new, iteration 7): a task's title cannot be changed by anybody -- TaskUpdate has no title field, the drawer has no editor. Filed not fixed: gap or contract is the operator's call. Worth telling them that F116's RequestModel base is what surfaced it, by turning a silent 200 into a 422 naming the field, within a day of shipping.

F123 (new, iteration 6): a job firing crashed out reads `failed` forever, including after the Hub's own crash recovery retried the work on the same conversation and it COMPLETED -- and no row records the retry. Mechanism is one line (finalize_job_run_for_conversation matches only status == 'in_progress'). Deliberately unfixed: it is a decision about what a JobRun is, and F121 is open against the same table for the same firing/turn/work confusion. Decide them together. Three shapes costed in FINDINGS.md with a recommendation.

An interrupted run's `ended_at` is the RESTART time, not the crash time, so a run's duration read from the database is inflated by the whole outage. Harmless today -- `ended_at` is on no response schema and no UI component reads it -- and a nine-hour outage would report a nine-hour run to whoever surfaces it first. The honest upper bound the Hub still holds is the last agent_outputs row for the run.

F116 is closed and archived (openspec/changes/archive/2026-08-29-an-unknown-field-is-named/). The method finding is worth more than the fix: three rounds in a row the defect was the ENUMERATION, not the code -- round 2 found round 1's, round 3 found round 2's, and the full suite found round 3's. None was found by re-reading the previous round; each was found by re-deriving the population by a different route. Worth telling the operator, and worth applying to the next spec loop: ask what population the argument rests on, then derive it twice.
